statement: The fixed C.34 median prescription need not extend equivariantly over an adjacent open orbit. An explicit plane R2-action has a based ambient-null centralizer loop whose median edge translations are (1,0,0), while the exact boundary restriction morphism from the open-orbit centralizer is (A,B) maps to (A,B,A-B). The original loop has an explicit global equivariant contraction.
where_proved: Part C, statement C.35; work/part_b/c35.tex; exact endpoint calculation in work/part_b/code/c35_median_extension_certificate.py and its JSON output
depends_on: C.27 median formula; C.34 full nonopen-locus continuity; explicit simplex action and its logarithmic coordinate homeomorphism; doubling a closed disc gives a sphere; deletion of a fixed point gives a plane; exact linear restriction and annihilator maps
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b) infinite-operator request; obstruction to extending a fixed contraction prescription in the C.12 proof route
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. This is an obstruction to one specified extension prescription, with the exact restriction morphism proved. It does not assert a level-0 comparison failure; the original loop's global null-homotopy is displayed.
notes: The projective positive-diagonal action on a simplex has interior translations (a,b) and edge characters a,b,a-b. Doubling and removing a fixed vertex produces a plane action with two open orbits, three line orbits and two fixed points. The parameter loop 0 to (1,1) to (1,0) to 0 generates all of R2 and contracts by real scaling. At median prefix r=1/3 and current time t=2/3, the edge values are (1,0,0). Their annihilator residual for the actual restriction image is 1. The code computes all these values using fractions. General global assembly must allow changing the nonopen-locus contraction. C36 and C37 satisfy the exact boundary equations on the closed union X2 of dimension-two proper-image open orbits, including infinite accumulation. Extension across X2 to its exterior and the other proper operator cases remains unresolved in C12.
